heuristics: H1 (mixing): the constants c_j = jQ + 2^j mod r have pairwise differences spanning 0.9688 of the modulus (verified in Part A), so the scalar difference walk between two walkers wraps mod r and walker states collide at the standard parallel-rho birthday rate t^2/(2(r-1)) (van Oorschot-Wiener); the toy measures 0.867 of the all-pair ideal and 0.99 of the cross-pair ideal. Pure power-of-two constants fail this at production scale (the difference walk does not wrap) and are not used.

Efficiency floor 0.75: below the toy-measured ratio by 25%, consistent with Teske's r-adding-walk analysis for r = 32; the claimed success is computed at this floor (0.4066249787 >= 0.39) and does not depend on the measurement beyond the floor's support.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution is claimed or possible.
Single-shot randomized attack at the 0.39 threshold (modeled success 0.4066 at the 0.75 efficiency floor).
The distinguished-point table is a hard 2^97-slot allocation (2^104 bytes); overflow aborts with probability <= exp(-2^94.4), subtracted.

Standard cryptanalysis (parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points); the provable cycle-freedom of the mixed-radix constants c_j = jQ + 2^j and the full-coverage ledger are the contribution under this cost model.
